# Where a frame lands on the 720x480 raster, for jfplay's geometry
# (arm/video_geometry.h, tested by arm/test_video_geometry.c) and the app's
# calibration (app/internal/ui/geometry.go Fit). Both test suites read this
# file, so the pattern the app draws and the picture jfplay shows cannot
# drift apart.
#
# left top right bottom width   aspect      lines   x   y   w   h
# (edges inside the raster's; width in thousandths; aspect as a fraction;
# lines is the frame's own height)

# the whole raster: every frame lands as it did before calibration existed
0 0 0 0 1000        640/480     480     0   0   720 480   # 4:3
0 0 0 0 1000        4/3         480     0   0   720 480   # 4:3 DVD, aspect from the header
0 0 0 0 1000        644/480     480     0   0   720 480   # a hair wider than 4:3: lines kept 1:1
0 0 0 0 1000        636/480     480     0   0   720 480   # a hair narrower: no side slivers
0 0 0 0 1000        630/480     480     0   0   720 480   # narrower still, within 12 pixels of full width
0 0 0 0 1000        629/480     480     0   0   720 480
0 0 0 0 1000        628/480     480     6   0   706 480   # beyond that: pillarbox
0 0 0 0 1000        652/480     480     0   0   720 480   # wider: its 480 lines kept 1:1
0 0 0 0 1000        656/480     480     0   6   720 468   # beyond 2%: letterbox
0 0 0 0 1000        636/476     476     0   2   720 476   # near 4:3 with its own 476 lines kept
0 0 0 0 1000        648/360     360     0   60  720 360   # 360 lines kept rather than 356
0 0 0 0 1000        720/404     404     0   60  720 360   # 16:9
0 0 0 0 1000        16/9        480     0   60  720 360   # anamorphic 16:9 DVD
0 0 0 0 1000        720/306     306     0   104 720 272   # 2.35:1
0 0 0 0 1000        480/360     360     0   0   720 480   # small 4:3
0 0 0 0 1000        6/5         480     36  0   648 480   # narrower than 4:3: pillarbox
0 0 0 0 1000        270/480     480     208 0   304 480   # portrait
0 0 0 0 1000        1290/960    960     0   2   720 476   # a hair wider than 4:3, far from 480 lines
0 0 0 0 1000        484/360     360     0   2   720 476
0 0 0 0 1000        1920/18     18      0   230 720 18    # the smallest height, lines 1:1

# edges moved in for overscan: each frame keeps the shape it has on the whole
# raster, as large as fits the area
16 12 16 12 1000    4/3         480     18  12  684 456   # 4:3 fills the height
16 12 16 12 1000    720/404     404     16  68  688 344   # 16:9 fills the width
20 10 8 14 1000     4/3         480     24  10  684 456   # off-centre set
16 10 16 10 1000    4/3         480     16  10  688 460   # two lines short of the area: fill it
0 4 0 4 1000        4/3         480     6   4   708 472   # 480 lines don't fit: scaled, not cut
0 2 0 6 1000        636/476     476     2   2   714 472   # a 720:476 picture, scaled into 472 lines
0 2 0 2 1000        636/476     476     0   2   720 476   # into exactly 476 it goes 1:1
120 80 120 80 1150  720/306     306     120 160 480 158   # the limits

# width corrected for a set that draws too wide or too narrow
0 0 0 0 980         4/3         480     6   0   706 480   # too wide: narrower picture
0 0 0 0 980         636/476     476     4   0   712 480   # the 720:476 shape, narrowed
0 0 0 0 1020        4/3         480     0   4   720 470   # too narrow: can't widen, so shorter
0 0 0 0 1010        644/480     480     0   2   720 476   # not snapped back to 480 lines
0 0 0 0 1020        720/404     404     0   64  720 352
0 0 0 0 850         270/480     480     230 0   258 480
